headline: Father and brother of prime accused in Rangpur 4-murder case released after DIB questioning
summary: Binay Das and Parth Das, father and elder brother of Siddharth Das, were released on bond after 4.5 hours of interrogation by the Detective Branch regarding the sensational quadruple murder in Rangpur.
details: Binay Das and Parth Das, father and elder brother of Siddharth Das, the prime accused in the sensational Rangpur quadruple murder case, were released by the Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) after 4.5 hours of interrogation. They were released around midnight on Saturday after signing a bond.

The two were detained from their home in Masuapara earlier that evening for questioning. Deputy Police Commissioner Sanatan Chakraborty stated that they had been repeatedly summoned via phone and DB members but failed to appear, necessitating their detention.

Prior to their detention, Parth Das and Binay Das allegedly stopped a journalist's motorcycle, snatched the keys, and assaulted him. Parth Das was seen limping upon release, though he claimed it was due to an injury sustained while resisting arrest, not from physical abuse by the DB.

Both Binay and Parth Das stated they were initially anxious but felt reassured after arriving at the DB office. They answered various questions and were released after promising to cooperate with future interrogations as needed for the investigation.

The four victims — retired school teacher Ganapati Chakraborty Jewel, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty Bola, daughter Agami Chakraborty Prarthi, and son Ayush Chakraborty Priyam — were found murdered in their Masuapara home on August 22.

Ganapati Chakraborty's elder brother filed a murder case, leading to the arrest of neighbors Siddharth Das and Mugdho Das on August 23. Both confessed to the killings under Section 164, stating the murders occurred after the victims witnessed them consuming Yaba.

The police are conducting DNA dope tests on the accused and forensic examinations on 35 seized items. Public protests demanding proper investigation and justice continue in Rangpur, with the Lawyers' Association refusing to represent the accused.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman calls for global unity against enforced disappearances, accountability
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged worldwide cooperation to ensure justice and accountability for those involved in enforced disappearances, describing them as heinous acts. His comments come ahead of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disap
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for global unity and solidarity to ensure justice and accountability for individuals and institutions involved in enforced disappearances. He termed such acts as "heinous and gruesome."

The Prime Minister noted that enforced disappearances are particularly prevalent in countries ruled by autocratic regimes, often used to suppress anti-government movements. His remarks were made on the eve of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances.

The United Nations has observed August 30 as the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances since 2011. The day aims to raise global awareness, trace missing people, and show solidarity with their families.

Tarique Rahman stated that the ousted "fascist" government resorted to inhumane practices, including enforced disappearances and abductions. Many individuals were reportedly detained for months or years in centers known as 'Aynaghar'.

Citing international human rights organizations, he mentioned that law enforcement agencies allegedly disappeared over 700 people during the deposed regime. He emphasized that a disappearance shatters the hopes and dreams of entire families.
To combat these crimes, the current government has initiated trials after investigating each incident. A legal framework is also being prepared to prevent such occurrences in the future.

Earlier, at an event, the Prime Minister handed over job appointment letters to 74 members of families affected by enforced disappearances and killings, as well as the July uprising. He pledged his government's commitment to fulfilling the aspirations of those who sacrificed for independence and democracy.
Among the recipients were family members of Iftekhar Ahmed Dinar, Nuruzzaman Jony, Anwar Hossain Mahbub, Selim Reza Pintu, and Khaled Hossain Sohel, alongside those affected by the July uprising.
